definition: A root that cannot be written as a whole number or a fraction, such as $\sqrt{2}$, left as a root to keep it exact; it is simplest when the number under the root has no square factor except $1$, as in $\sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5}$.
Rewriting a fraction so that its denominator has no surd, by multiplying the top and bottom by the same number, such as $\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}} = \frac{3\sqrt{5}}{5}$.
